The decrease in 2022, compared to 2021, is primarily due to discontinued patient therapies at Kroger Specialty Pharmacy. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:2.09pt 0pt 0pt 6.35pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:0pt;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Merchandise Costs&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The &#x201c;Merchandise costs&#x201d; line item of the Consolidated Statements of Operations includes product costs, net of discounts and allowances; advertising costs (see separate discussion below); inbound freight charges; warehousing costs, including receiving and inspection costs; transportation costs; and food production and operational costs.&#160; Warehousing, transportation and manufacturing management salaries are also included in the &#x201c;Merchandise costs&#x201d; line item; however, purchasing management salaries and administration costs are included in the &#x201c;OG&amp;amp;A&#x201d; line item along with most of the Company&#x2019;s other managerial and administrative costs.&#160; Shipping and delivery costs associated with the Company&#x2019;s digital offerings originating from non-retail store locations are included in the &#x201c;Merchandise costs&#x201d; line item.  Rent expense and depreciation and amortization expense are shown separately in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;Warehousing and transportation costs include distribution center direct wages, transportation direct wages, repairs and maintenance, utilities, inbound freight and, where applicable, third-party warehouse management fees.&#160; These costs are recognized in the periods the related expenses are incurred.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company believes the classification of costs included in merchandise costs could vary widely throughout the industry.&#160; The Company&#x2019;s approach is to include in the &#x201c;Merchandise costs&#x201d; line item the direct, net costs of acquiring products and making them available to customers.&#160; The Company believes this approach most accurately presents the actual costs of products sold.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company recognizes all vendor allowances as a reduction in merchandise costs when the related product is sold.&#160; When possible, vendor allowances are applied to the related product cost by item and, therefore, reduce the carrying value of inventory by item.&#160; When the items are sold, the vendor allowance is recognized.&#160; When it is not possible, due to systems constraints, to allocate vendor allowances to the product by item, vendor allowances are recognized as a reduction in merchandise costs based on inventory turns and, therefore, recognized as the product is sold.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Advertising Costs&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company&#x2019;s advertising costs are recognized in the periods the related expenses are incurred and are included in the &#x201c;Merchandise costs&#x201d; line item of the Consolidated Statements of Operations.&#160; The Company&#x2019;s advertising costs totaled $1,089 in 2023, $1,030 in 2022 and $984 in 2021.&#160; The Company does not record vendor allowances for co-operative advertising as a reduction of advertising expense.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;min-height:12.0pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Operating, General and Administrative Expenses&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;min-height:12.0pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;OG&amp;amp;A expenses consist primarily of employee-related costs such as wages, healthcare benefit costs, retirement plan costs, utilities, and credit card fees. Shipping and delivery costs associated with the Company's digital offerings originating from retail store locations, including third-party delivery fees, are included in the &#x201c;OG&amp;amp;A&#x201d; line item of the Consolidated Statements of Operations.  Rent expense, depreciation and amortization expense and interest expense are shown separately in the Consolidated Statement of Operations.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;For purposes of the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, the Company considers all highly liquid debt instruments purchased with an original maturity of three months or less to be temporary cash investments.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Segments&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The Company operates supermarkets, multi-department stores and fulfillment centers throughout the United States.  The Company&#x2019;s retail operations, which represent &lt;/span&gt;97%&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; of the Company&#x2019;s consolidated sales, are its only reportable segment.  The Company aggregates its operating divisions into &lt;/span&gt;one&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; reportable segment due to the operating divisions having similar economic characteristics with similar long-term financial performance.  In addition, the Company&#x2019;s operating divisions offer customers similar products, have similar distribution methods, operate in similar regulatory environments, purchase the majority of the merchandise for retail sale from similar (and in many cases identical) vendors on a coordinated basis from a centralized location, serve similar types of customers, and are allocated capital from a centralized location.  Operating divisions are organized primarily on a geographical basis so that the operating division management team can be responsive to local needs of the operating division and can execute company strategic plans and initiatives throughout the locations in their operating division. This geographical separation is the primary differentiation between these retail operating divisions.  The geographical basis of organization reflects how the business is managed and how the Company&#x2019;s Chief Executive Officer, who acts as the Company&#x2019;s chief operating decision maker, assesses performance internally.  All of the Company&#x2019;s operations are domestic.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</us-gaap:OrganizationConsolidationBasisOfPresentationBusinessDescriptionAndAccountingPoliciesTextBlock>

Replacement cost was higher than the carrying amount by &lt;/span&gt;$2,309 at February 3, 2024 and $2,196 at January 28, 2023.&#160; The Company follows the Link-Chain, Dollar-Value LIFO method for purposes of calculating its LIFO charge.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt; &#160;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The item-cost method of accounting to determine inventory cost before the LIFO adjustment is followed for substantially all store inventories at the Company&#x2019;s supermarket divisions.&#160; This method involves counting each item in inventory, assigning costs to each of these items based on the actual purchase costs (net of vendor allowances and cash discounts) of each item and recording the cost of items sold.&#160;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The item-cost method of accounting allows for more accurate reporting of periodic inventory balances and enables management to more precisely manage inventory.  In addition, substantially all of the Company&#x2019;s inventory consists of finished goods and is recorded at actual purchase costs (net of vendor allowances and cash discounts).&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The Company evaluates inventory shortages throughout the year based on actual physical counts in its facilities.       id="Tb_ubEjkemBnEWnCC7iLw7ICA">&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Leases&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The Company leases certain store real estate, warehouses, distribution centers, fulfillment centers, office space and equipment.  The Company determines if an arrangement is a lease at inception.  Finance and operating lease assets and liabilities are recognized at the lease commencement date.  Finance and operating lease liabilities represent the present value of minimum lease payments not yet paid. Operating lease assets represent the right to use an underlying asset and are based upon the operating lease liabilities adjusted for prepayments, lease incentives and impairment, if any. To determine the present value of lease payments, the Company estimates an incremental borrowing rate which represents the rate used for a secured borrowing of a similar term as the lease.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;Lease terms generally range from 10 to 20 years with options to renew for &lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_myk3DgPsa0e4VZ5Nh0JfiA;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;"&gt;varying&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_QdWUUpWqgUiLwVyUynF1Ag;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;"&gt;terms&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; at the Company&#x2019;s sole discretion. The lease term includes the initial contractual term as well as any options to extend the lease when it is reasonably certain that the Company will exercise that option. Leases with an initial term of 12 months or less are not recorded on the balance sheet.  Certain leases include escalation clauses or payment of executory costs such as property taxes, utilities or insurance and maintenance.  Operating lease payments are charged on a straight-line basis to rent expense over the lease term and finance lease payments are charged to interest expense and depreciation and amortization expense over the lease term.  Assets under finance leases are amortized in accordance with the Company&#x2019;s normal depreciation policy for owned assets or over the lease term, if shorter.  The Company&#x2019;s lease agreements do not contain any residual value guarantees or material restrictive covenants.  For additional information on leases, see Note 9 to the Consolidated Financial Statements.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</us-gaap:LesseeLeasesPolicyTextBlock>

With respect to owned property and equipment held for disposal, the value of the property and equipment is adjusted to reflect recoverable values based on previous efforts to dispose of similar assets and current economic conditions.&#160; Impairment is recognized for the excess of the carrying value over the estimated fair market value, reduced by estimated direct costs of disposal.       id="Tb_hnIoEeeml0ifJ82onFWflg">&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Uncertain Tax Positions&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The Company reviews the tax positions taken or expected to be taken on tax returns to determine whether and to what extent a benefit can be recognized in its consolidated financial statements.  Refer to Note 4 for the amount of unrecognized tax benefits and other related disclosures related to uncertain tax positions.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="margin-bottom:6pt;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;Various taxing authorities periodically audit the Company&#x2019;s income tax returns.&#160; These audits include questions regarding the Company&#x2019;s tax filing positions, including the timing and amount of deductions and the allocation of income to various tax jurisdictions.&#160; In evaluating the exposures connected with these various tax filing positions, including state and local taxes, the Company records allowances for probable exposures.&#160; A number of years may elapse before a particular matter, for which an allowance has been established, is audited and fully resolved.&#160; As of February 3, 2024, the years ended February 1, 2020 and forward remain open for review for federal income tax purposes.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The assessment of the Company&#x2019;s tax position relies on the judgment of management to estimate the exposures associated with the Company&#x2019;s various filing positions.&lt;/p&gt;</us-gaap:IncomeTaxUncertaintiesPolicy>

Pharmacy sales&lt;/span&gt; are&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt; recorded when the &lt;/span&gt;product is&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;provided &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;to&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;the&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; customer.  Digital channel originated sales are recognized either upon pickup in store or upon delivery to the customer.  &lt;/span&gt;Amounts billed to a customer related to shipping and delivery represent revenues earned for the goods provided and are classified as sales.&#160;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; When shipping is discounted, it is recorded as an adjustment to sales.  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;Discounts provided&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;to customers&lt;/span&gt; by&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt; the Company&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;at&lt;/span&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;provided&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;in connection with&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;in sales&lt;/span&gt; as &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;the products &lt;/span&gt;are&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt; sold.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:2.45pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;Discounts provided &lt;/span&gt;by&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt; vendors, usually in&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;the&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;form&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;of&lt;span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"&gt;       id="Tb_UaBnLrLypEibWwFj5sJIpw">&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Merchandise Costs&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The &#x201c;Merchandise costs&#x201d; line item of the Consolidated Statements of Operations includes product costs, net of discounts and allowances; advertising costs (see separate discussion below); inbound freight charges; warehousing costs, including receiving and inspection costs; transportation costs; and food production and operational costs.&#160; Warehousing, transportation and manufacturing management salaries are also included in the &#x201c;Merchandise costs&#x201d; line item; however, purchasing management salaries and administration costs are included in the &#x201c;OG&amp;amp;A&#x201d; line item along with most of the Company&#x2019;s other managerial and administrative costs.&#160; Shipping and delivery costs associated with the Company&#x2019;s digital offerings originating from non-retail store locations are included in the &#x201c;Merchandise costs&#x201d; line item.  Rent expense and depreciation and amortization expense are shown separately in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;Warehousing and transportation costs include distribution center direct wages, transportation direct wages, repairs and maintenance, utilities, inbound freight and, where applicable, third-party warehouse management fees.&#160; These costs are recognized in the periods the related expenses are incurred.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company believes the classification of costs included in merchandise costs could vary widely throughout the industry.&#160; The Company&#x2019;s approach is to include in the &#x201c;Merchandise costs&#x201d; line item the direct, net costs of acquiring products and making them available to customers.&#160; The Company believes this approach most accurately presents the actual costs of products sold.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company recognizes all vendor allowances as a reduction in merchandise costs when the related product is sold.&#160; When possible, vendor allowances are applied to the related product cost by item and, therefore, reduce the carrying value of inventory by item.&#160; When the items are sold, the vendor allowance is recognized.&#160; When it is not possible, due to systems constraints, to allocate vendor allowances to the product by item, vendor allowances are recognized as a reduction in merchandise costs based on inventory turns and, therefore, recognized as the product is sold.&lt;/p&gt;</kr:MerchandiseCostsPolicyTextBlock>

    <us-gaap:SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock
      contextRef="Duration_1_29_2023_To_2_3_2024__weV9Aqkb0CzFGYumT_qEw"
      id="Tb_JqCXOwpVFkCimR2d0ieCaQ">&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Segments&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The Company operates supermarkets, multi-department stores and fulfillment centers throughout the United States.  The Company&#x2019;s retail operations, which represent &lt;/span&gt;97%&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; of the Company&#x2019;s consolidated sales, are its only reportable segment.  The Company aggregates its operating divisions into &lt;/span&gt;one&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; reportable segment due to the operating divisions having similar economic characteristics with similar long-term financial performance.  In addition, the Company&#x2019;s operating divisions offer customers similar products, have similar distribution methods, operate in similar regulatory environments, purchase the majority of the merchandise for retail sale from similar (and in many cases identical) vendors on a coordinated basis from a centralized location, serve similar types of customers, and are allocated capital from a centralized location.  Operating divisions are organized primarily on a geographical basis so that the operating division management team can be responsive to local needs of the operating division and can execute company strategic plans and initiatives throughout the locations in their operating division. This geographical separation is the primary differentiation between these retail operating divisions.  The geographical basis of organization reflects how the business is managed and how the Company&#x2019;s Chief Executive Officer, who acts as the Company&#x2019;s chief operating decision maker, assesses performance internally.  All of the Company&#x2019;s operations are domestic.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</us-gaap:SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock>

Further, based on the analysis described below, the Company has recorded a valuation allowance against some of the deferred tax assets resulting from its state credits.  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The Company regularly reviews all deferred tax assets on a tax filer and jurisdictional basis to estimate whether these assets are more likely than not to be realized based on all available evidence.  This evidence includes historical taxable income, projected future taxable income, the expected timing of the reversal of existing temporary differences and the implementation of tax planning strategies.  Projected future taxable income is based on expected results and assumptions as to the jurisdiction in which the income will be earned.  The expected timing of the reversals of existing temporary differences is based on current tax law and the Company&#x2019;s tax methods of accounting.  Unless deferred tax assets are more likely than not to be realized, a valuation allowance is established to reduce the carrying value of the deferred tax asset until such time that realization becomes more likely than not.  Increases and decreases in these valuation allowances are included in "Income tax expense" in the Consolidated Statements of Operations. &lt;/span&gt;As of February 3, 2024, January 28, 2023, and The Company is obligated to repurchase the properties at the end of the base term for &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRomanPSMT';"&gt;$300&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRomanPSMT';"&gt; if the lessor exercises its put option.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRomanPSMT';visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRomanPSMT';"&gt;On July 6, 2021, the Company entered into an amended and restated credit agreement, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRomanPSMT';"&gt;which credit agreement was further amended on November 9, 2022 (as so amended, the &#x201c;Credit Agreement&#x201d;) providing&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRomanPSMT';"&gt; for a &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRomanPSMT';"&gt;$2,750&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRomanPSMT';"&gt; unsecured revolving credit facility (the &#x201c;Revolving Credit Facility&#x201d;), with a termination date of July 6, 2026, unless extended as permitted under the Credit Agreement. The Company has the ability to increase the size of the Revolving Credit Facility by up to an additional &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRomanPSMT';"&gt;$1,250&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRomanPSMT';"&gt;, subject to certain conditions.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;Borrowings under the Credit Agreement bear interest, at the Company&#x2019;s option, at either (i) adjusted Term SOFR plus a market spread, based on the Company&#x2019;s Public Debt Rating or (ii) the base rate, defined as the highest of (a) the Federal Funds Rate plus 0.5%, (b) Bank of America&#x2019;s prime rate, and (c) one-month Term SOFR plus 1.0%, plus a market rate spread based on the Company&#x2019;s Public Debt Rating&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;.  The Company will also pay a Commitment Fee based on its Public Debt Rating and Letter of Credit fees equal to a market rate spread based on the Company&#x2019;s Public Debt Rating.  &#x201c;Public Debt Rating&#x201d; means, as of any date, the rating that has been most recently announced by either S&amp;amp;P or Moody&#x2019;s, as the case may be, for any class of non-credit enhanced long-term senior unsecured debt issued by the Company.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Credit Agreement contains a covenant, which, among other things, requires the maintenance of a Leverage Ratio of not greater than (i) 3.50:1.00 or (ii) upon the consummation of the proposed merger with Albertsons, 4.50 to 1.00, with step downs to 4.25:1.00, 4.00:1.00, 3.75:1.00 and 3.50&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;:1.00 effective at the end of the third, fifth, seventh and ninth, full fiscal quarters after the consummation of the proposed merger, respectively.  The Company may repay the Credit Agreement in whole or in part at any time without premium or penalty.  The Credit Agreement is not guaranteed by the Company&#x2019;s subsidiaries.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRomanPSMT';visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'TimesNewRomanPSMT';"&gt;On October 13, 2022, the Company entered into a merger agreement with Albertsons Companies, Inc. (&#x201c;Albertsons&#x201d;). For additional information about the Company&#x2019;s unsecured bridge term loan facility and term loan credit agreement associated with the merger agreement, see Note 16 to the Consolidated Financial Statements.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;As of February 3, 2024, and January 28, 2023, the Company had no commercial paper borrowings and no borrowings under the Credit Agreement.&lt;span style="color:#ff0000;white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#ff0000;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;As of February 3, 2024, the Company had outstanding letters of credit in the amount of $314, of which $2 reduces funds available under the Credit Agreement.     <us-gaap:DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock
      contextRef="Duration_1_29_2023_To_2_3_2024__weV9Aqkb0CzFGYumT_qEw"
      id="Tb_sx5yX0lAKUWgTJl6UbuGwQ">&lt;table style="border-collapse:collapse;border:0;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"&gt;&lt;b style="font-weight:bold;"&gt;6.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"&gt;&lt;b style="font-weight:bold;"&gt;DERIVATIVE FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;GAAP requires that derivatives be carried at fair value on the balance sheet and provides for hedge accounting when certain conditions are met.&#160; The Company&#x2019;s derivative financial instruments are recognized on the balance sheet at fair value.&#160; Changes in the fair value of derivative instruments designated as &#x201c;cash flow&#x201d; hedges, to the extent the hedges are highly effective, are recorded in other comprehensive income, net of tax effects.  Ineffective cash flow hedges, if any, are recognized in current period earnings.&#160; Other comprehensive income or loss is reclassified into current period earnings when the hedged transaction affects earnings.&#160; Changes in the fair value of derivative instruments designated as &#x201c;fair value&#x201d; hedges, along with corresponding changes in the fair values of the hedged assets or liabilities, are recorded in current period earnings.  Ineffective fair value hedges, if any, are recognized in current period earnings.  Changes in fair value of derivative instruments not designated as hedges are recognized in current period earnings and included in &#x201c;Gain (loss) on investments&#x201d; in the Company&#x2019;s Consolidated Statements of Operations.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company assesses, both at the inception of the hedge and on an ongoing basis, whether derivatives used as hedging instruments are highly effective in offsetting the changes in the fair value or cash flow of the hedged items. &#160;If it is determined that a derivative is not highly effective as a hedge or ceases to be highly effective, the Company discontinues hedge accounting prospectively.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Interest Rate Risk Management&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company is exposed to market risk from fluctuations in interest rates. The Company manages its exposure to interest rate fluctuations through the use of a commercial paper program, interest rate swaps (fair value hedges) and forward-starting interest rate swaps (cash flow hedges). The Company&#x2019;s current program relative to interest rate protection contemplates hedging the exposure to changes in the fair value of fixed-rate debt attributable to changes in interest rates. To do this, the Company uses the following guidelines: (i) use average daily outstanding borrowings to determine annual debt amounts subject to interest rate exposure, (ii) limit the average annual amount subject to interest rate reset and the amount of floating rate debt to a combined total amount that represents 25% of the carrying value of the Company&#x2019;s debt portfolio or less, (iii) include no leveraged products, and (iv) hedge without regard to profit motive or sensitivity to current mark-to-market status.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company reviews compliance with these guidelines annually with the Finance Committee of the Board of Directors.&#160; These guidelines may change as the Company&#x2019;s needs dictate.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="text-decoration-color:#000000;text-decoration-line:underline;text-decoration-style:solid;"&gt;Fair Value Interest Rate Swaps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company did not have any outstanding interest rate derivatives classified as fair value hedges as of February 3, 2024 and January 28, 2023.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="text-decoration-color:#000000;text-decoration-line:underline;text-decoration-style:solid;"&gt;Cash Flow Forward-Starting Interest Rate Swaps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;As of February 3, 2024 and January 28, 2023, the Company had five forward-starting interest rate swap agreements with a maturity date of August 1, 2027 with an aggregate notional amount totaling $5,350. A forward-starting interest rate swap is an agreement that effectively hedges the variability in future benchmark interest payments attributable to changes in interest rates on the forecasted issuance of fixed-rate debt. The Company entered into these forward-starting interest rate swaps in order to lock in fixed interest rates on its forecasted issuances of debt. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;A notional amount of $2,350 of these forward-starting interest rate swaps was designated as a cash-flow hedge as defined by GAAP. Accordingly, the changes in fair value of these forward-starting interest rate swaps are recorded to accumulated other comprehensive income and reclassified into net earnings when the hedged transaction affects net earnings. As of February 3, 2024, the fair value of the interest rate swaps designated as cash flow hedges was recorded in &#x201c;Other Assets&#x201d; for $125 and accumulated other comprehensive income for $95, net of tax. &#160;As of January 28, 2023, the fair value of the interest rate swaps designated as cash flow hedges was recorded in &#x201c;Other long-term liabilities&#x201d; for $116 and accumulated other comprehensive loss for $89, net of tax.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The remainder of the notional amount of $3,000 of the forward-starting interest rate swaps was not designated as a cash-flow hedge. Accordingly, the changes in the fair value of these forward-starting interest rate swaps not designated as cash-flow hedges are recognized through net earnings. As of February 3, 2024, the fair value of these swaps was recorded in &#x201c;Other Assets&#x201d; for $35 and &#x201c;Other long-term liabilities&#x201d; for $3. In 2023, the Company recognized an unrealized gain of $174 related to these swaps that is included in &#x201c;Gain (loss) on investments&#x201d; in the Company&#x2019;s Consolidated Statements of Operations. As of January 28, 2023, the fair value of these swaps was recorded in &#x201c;Other long-term liabilities&#x201d; for $142. In 2022, the Company recognized an unrealized loss of $142 related to these swaps that is included in &#x201c;Gain (loss) on investments&#x201d; in the Company&#x2019;s Consolidated Statements of Operations.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The following table summarizes the effect of the Company&#x2019;s derivative instruments designated &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;For the above cash flow interest rate swaps, the Company has entered into International Swaps and Derivatives Association master netting agreements that permit the net settlement of amounts owed under their respective derivative contracts.  Under these master netting agreements, net settlement generally permits the Company or the counterparty to determine the net amount payable for contracts due on the same date and in the same currency for similar types of derivative transactions.  These master netting agreements generally also provide for net settlement of all outstanding contracts with a counterparty in the case of an event of default or a termination event.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;background:#00ffff;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;Collateral is generally not required of the counterparties or of the Company under these master netting agreements. As of February 3, 2024, no cash collateral was received or pledged under the master netting agreements.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The Company values interest rate hedges using observable forward yield curves.  These forward yield curves are classified as Level 2 inputs. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;Fair value measurements of non-financial assets and non-financial liabilities are primarily used in the impairment analysis of goodwill, other intangible assets, long-lived assets and in the valuation of store lease exit costs.  The Company reviews goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible assets for impairment annually, during the fourth quarter of each fiscal year, and as circumstances indicate the possibility of impairment.  See Note 2 for further discussion related to the Company&#x2019;s carrying value of goodwill.  Long-lived assets and store lease exit costs were measured at fair value on a nonrecurring basis using Level 3 inputs as defined in the fair value hierarchy.  See Note 1 for further discussion of the Company&#x2019;s policies for impairments of long-lived assets and valuation of store lease exit costs.  In 2023, long-lived assets with a carrying amount of &lt;/span&gt;$72 were written down to their fair value of $3, resulting in an impairment charge of $69. In 2022, long-lived assets with a carrying amount of $69 were written down to their fair value of $1, resulting in an impairment charge of $68.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight:bold;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;Fair Value of Other Financial Instruments&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Current and Long-term Debt&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The fair value of the Company&#x2019;s long-term debt, including current maturities, was estimated based on the quoted market prices for the same or similar issues adjusted for illiquidity based on available market evidence.  If quoted market prices were not available, the fair value was based upon the net present value of the future cash flow using the forward interest rate yield curve in effect at respective year-ends.  At February 3, 2024, the fair value of total debt excluding obligations under finance leases was &lt;/span&gt;$9,401 compared to a carrying value of $10,187&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;.  At January 28, 2023, the fair value of total debt excluding obligations under finance leases was &lt;/span&gt;$10,593 compared to a carrying value of $11,292.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Contingent Consideration&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="background:#ffffff;"&gt;As a result of the Home Chef merger in 2018, the Company recognized a contingent liability of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="background:#ffffff;"&gt;$91&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;background:#ffffff;"&gt; on the acquisition date.  The contingent consideration was measured using unobservable (Level 3) inputs and was included in &lt;/span&gt;&#x201c;Other long-term liabilities&#x201d; within the Consolidated Balance Sheet&lt;span style="background:#ffffff;"&gt;.&#160;The Company estimated the fair value of the earnout liability by applying a &lt;/span&gt;Monte-Carlo simulation method&lt;span style="background:#ffffff;"&gt; using the Company&#x2019;s projection of future operating results for both the online and offline businesses related to the Home Chef merger and the estimated probability of achievement of the earnout target metrics.&#160;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;The Monte-Carlo simulation is a generally accepted statistical technique used to generate a defined number of valuation paths in order to develop a reasonable estimate of the fair value of the earnout liability.&lt;span style="background:#ffffff;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The liability is remeasured to fair value using the Monte-Carlo simulation method at each reporting period, and the change in fair value, including accretion for the passage of time, is recognized in net earnings until the contingency is resolved.  In 2020, the Company amended the contingent consideration agreement including the performance milestones to align with the Company&#x2019;s current business strategies.  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="background:#ffffff;"&gt;In 2022, the Company recorded adjustments to increase the contingent consideration liability for &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="background:#ffffff;"&gt;$20&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="background:#ffffff;"&gt; in OG&amp;amp;A. &lt;/span&gt;During 2023, the Company made the final contingent consideration payment of $83 which was based on the fair value of the outstanding year-end 2022 liability.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Cash and Temporary Cash Investments, Store Deposits In-Transit, Receivables, Prepaid and Other Current Assets, Accounts Payable, Accrued Salaries and Wages and Other Current Liabilities&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The carrying amounts of these items approximated fair value due to their short-term nature.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Other Assets&lt;/i&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:9.35pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The fair value of certain financial instruments, measured using Level 1 inputs, was $578 and $401 as of February 3, 2024 and January 28, 2023, respectively, and is included in &#x201c;Other assets&#x201d; in the Company&#x2019;s Consolidated Balance Sheets. The unrealized loss for these Level 1 investments was approximately $66 and $586 for 2023 and 2022, respectively, and is included in &#x201c;Gain (loss) on investments&#x201d; in the Company&#x2019;s Consolidated Statements of Operations. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company held other equity investments without a readily determinable fair value. These investments are measured initially at cost and remeasured for observable price changes to fair value through net earnings. The value of these investments was $92 and $320&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; as of February 3, 2024 and January 28, 2023, respectively, and is included in &#x201c;Other assets&#x201d; in the Company&#x2019;s Consolidated Balance Sheets.  The decrease in the value of these other equity investments without a readily determinable fair value was the result of one of the Company&#x2019;s investments now being measured using Level 1 inputs.  There were &lt;/span&gt;no other observable price changes or impairments for these investments without a readily determinable fair value during 2023 or 2022, and as such, they are excluded from the fair value measurements table above for February 3, 2024 and January 28, 2023.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span The Company&#x2019;s lease agreements do not contain any material residual value guarantees or material restrictive covenants.     <us-gaap:DisclosureOfCompensationRelatedCostsShareBasedPaymentsTextBlock
      contextRef="Duration_1_29_2023_To_2_3_2024__weV9Aqkb0CzFGYumT_qEw"
      id="Tb_EVmpiLTfd0SPeSZBCcahbA">&lt;table style="border-collapse:collapse;border:0;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"&gt;&lt;b style="font-weight:bold;"&gt;11.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"&gt;&lt;b style="font-weight:bold;"&gt;STOCK-BASED COMPENSATION&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company recognizes compensation expense for all share-based payments granted. The Company recognizes share-based compensation expense, net of an estimated forfeiture rate, over the requisite service period of the award based on the fair value at the date of the grant. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company grants options for common shares (&#x201c;stock options&#x201d;) to employees under various plans at an option price equal to the fair market value of the underlying shares on the grant date of the award. The Company accounts for stock options under the fair value recognition provisions. Stock options typically expire 10 years from the date of grant. Stock options vest between &lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_FwMeXsViVkSgXU64RC09fA;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;"&gt;one&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; and four years from the date of grant. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;In addition to the stock options described above, the Company awards restricted stock to employees and incentive shares to nonemployee directors under various plans. The restrictions on the restricted share awards generally lapse between &lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_aApILSjkV0a9XR80Ysu35A;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;"&gt;one&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt; and four years&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; from the date of the awards.  The Company determines the fair value for restricted stock awards in an amount equal to the fair market value of the underlying shares on the grant date of the award.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;At February 3, 2024, approximately 40 million common shares were available for future options or restricted stock grants under the 2019 Amended and Restated Long-Term Incentive Plan. Options granted reduce the shares available under the Plans at a ratio of one&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; to one.  Restricted stock grants reduce the shares available under the Plans at a ratio of &lt;/span&gt;2.83 to one.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;Equity awards granted are based on the aggregate value of the award on the grant date. This can affect the number of shares granted in a given year as equity awards. Excess tax benefits related to equity awards are recognized in the provision for income taxes. Equity awards may be approved at one of four meetings of its Board of Directors occurring shortly after the Company&#x2019;s release of quarterly earnings. The 2023 primary grants were made in conjunction with the March and June meetings of the Company&#x2019;s Board of Directors.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;All awards become immediately exercisable upon certain changes of control of the Company.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The weighted-average grant date fair value of stock options granted during 2023, 2022 and 2021 was $15.17, $15.91 and $8.54&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;, respectively.  The fair value of each stock option grant was estimated on the date of grant using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model, based on the assumptions shown in the table below.  The Black-Scholes model utilizes accounting judgment and financial estimates, including the term option holders are expected to retain their stock options before exercising them, the volatility of the Company&#x2019;s share price over that expected term, the dividend yield over the term and the number of awards expected to be forfeited before they vest.  Using alternative assumptions in the calculation of fair value would produce fair values for stock option grants that could be different than those used to record stock-based compensation expense in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.  The decrease in the fair value of the stock options granted during 2023, compared to 2022, resulted primarily from decreases in the Company&#x2019;s share price, partially offset by an increase in the weighted-average risk-free interest rate.  The increase in the fair value of the stock options granted during 2022, compared to 2021, resulted primarily from increases in the Company&#x2019;s share price, the weighted-average expected volatility, and an increase in the weighted-average risk-free interest rate.  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span       id="Tb_SaM-wYw-nU6zY84GlFI7kg">&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-weight:bold;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;table style="border-collapse:collapse;border:0;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:text-top;white-space:nowrap;width:18pt;padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"&gt;&lt;b style="font-weight:bold;"&gt;12.&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;"&gt;&lt;b style="font-weight:bold;"&gt;COMMITMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company continuously evaluates contingencies based upon the best available evidence.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company believes that allowances for loss have been provided to the extent necessary and that its assessment of contingencies is reasonable.&#160; To the extent that resolution of contingencies results in amounts that vary from the Company&#x2019;s estimates, future earnings will be charged or credited.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The principal contingencies are described below:&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Insurance&lt;/i&gt; &#x2014; The Company&#x2019;s workers&#x2019; compensation risks are self-insured in most states. In addition, other workers&#x2019; compensation risks and certain levels of insured general liability risks are based on retrospective premium plans, deductible plans and self-insured retention plans.&#160; The liability for workers&#x2019; compensation risks is accounted for on a present value basis.&#160; Actual claim settlements and expenses incident thereto may differ from the provisions for loss.&#160; Property risks have been underwritten by a subsidiary and are all reinsured with unrelated insurance companies.&#160; Operating divisions and subsidiaries have paid premiums, and the insurance subsidiary has provided loss allowances, based upon actuarially determined estimates.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Litigation&lt;/i&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; &#x2014; Various claims and lawsuits arising in the normal course of business, including personal injury, contract disputes, employment discrimination, wage and hour and other regulatory claims are pending against the Company.  Some of these suits purport or have been determined to be class actions and/or seek substantial damages.  Although it is not possible at this time to evaluate the merits of all of these claims and lawsuits, nor their likelihood of success, the Company is of the belief that any resulting liability will not have a material effect on the Company&#x2019;s financial position, results of operations, or cash flows.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company continually evaluates its exposure to loss contingencies arising from pending or threatened litigation and believes it has made provisions where it is reasonably possible to estimate and when an adverse outcome is probable.&#160; Nonetheless, assessing and predicting the outcomes of these matters involves substantial uncertainties.&#160; Management currently believes that the aggregate range of loss for the Company&#x2019;s exposure is not material to the Company.&#160; It remains possible that despite management&#x2019;s current belief, material differences in actual outcomes or changes in management&#x2019;s evaluation or predictions could arise that could have a material adverse effect on the Company&#x2019;s financial condition, results of operations, or cash flows.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company is one of dozens of companies that have been named in various lawsuits alleging that defendants contributed to create a public nuisance through the distribution and dispensing of opioids. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;On September 8, 2023, the Company announced that it reached an agreement in principle with plaintiffs to settle the majority of opioid claims that have been or could be brought against Kroger by states in which they operate, subdivisions, and Native American tribes.&#160; Along with the execution of certain non-monetary conditions that remain under discussion, the Company has agreed to pay up to $1,200 to states and subdivisions and $36 to Native American tribes in funding for abatement efforts, and approximately $177 to cover attorneys&#x2019; fees and costs. States, subdivisions, and the Native American tribes will have an opportunity to opt-in to participate in the settlement, and the Company will have full discretion to determine whether there is sufficient participation for the settlement to become effective. If all conditions are satisfied, the settlement would allow for the full resolution of all claims on behalf of participating states, subdivisions and Native American tribes and is not an admission of any wrongdoing or liability.&#160;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;As a result, the Company concluded that the agreement in principle for the settlement of opioid claims was probable, and for which the related loss was reasonably estimable. Accordingly, in 2023, the Company recognized opioid settlement charges of $1,413, $1,113 net of tax, relating to the nationwide opioid settlement framework. This charge is included in &#x201c;Operating, general and administrative&#x201d; in the Company&#x2019;s Consolidated Statement of Operations.&#160; &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The agreement in principle described above includes payments of approximately $1,236 and $177, in equal installments over 11 years and 6 years, respectively.&#160; As of February 3, 2024, the Company recorded $284 and $1,129 of the estimated settlement liability in &#x201c;Other current liabilities&#x201d; and &#x201c;Other long-term liabilities,&#x201d; respectively, in the Company&#x2019;s Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160; The current portion of the estimated settlement liability is recorded in &#x201c;Accrued expenses&#x201d; and the long-term portion of the estimated settlement liability is recorded in &#x201c;Other&#x201d; within &#x201c;Changes in operating assets and liabilities&#x201d; in the Company&#x2019;s Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows for fiscal year 2023. &lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;Because of the conditions remaining to satisfy, the Company cannot predict if the agreement will become effective, and whether unfavorable developments may occur. The amount of the actual loss may differ materially from the accrual estimate recorded as of February 3, 2024.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;Additionally, in 2023, the Company recorded a charge of $62 relating to a settlement of opioid litigation claims with the State of West Virginia. The agreed upon settlement framework resolves all opioid lawsuits and claims by the West Virginia Attorney General.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;In 2022, the Company recorded a charge of $85 relating to a settlement of opioid litigation claims with the State of New Mexico. The agreed upon settlement framework allocates $85 among various constituents related to the state of New Mexico. This settlement agreement resolved all opioid lawsuits and claims by the state of New Mexico against the Company.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The foregoing settlements are not admissions of wrongdoing or liability by the Company and the Company will continue to vigorously defend against any other claims and lawsuits relating to opioids that the settlements do not resolve.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-style:italic;visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;i style="font-style:italic;"&gt;Assignments &#x2014;&lt;/i&gt; The Company is contingently liable for leases that have been assigned to various third parties in connection with facility closings and dispositions.&#160; The Company could be required to satisfy the obligations under the leases if any of the assignees is unable to fulfill its lease obligations.&#160; Due to the wide distribution of the Company&#x2019;s assignments among third parties, and various other remedies available, the Company believes the likelihood that it will be required to assume a material amount of these obligations is remote.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureTextBlock>

These include several qualified pension plans (the &#x201c;Qualified Plans&#x201d;) and non-qualified pension plans (the &#x201c;Non-Qualified Plans&#x201d;).  The Non-Qualified Plans pay benefits to any employee that earns in excess of the maximum allowed for the Qualified Plans by Section 415 of the Internal Revenue Code.  The Company only funds obligations under the Qualified Plans.  Funding for the company-sponsored pension plans is based on a review of the specific requirements and on evaluation of the assets and liabilities of each plan.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;In addition to providing pension benefits, the Company provides certain health care benefits for retired employees. style="vertical-align:bottom;white-space:nowrap;width:3.41%;margin:0pt;padding:0pt;"&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company&#x2019;s discount rate assumptions were intended to reflect the rates at which the pension benefits could be effectively settled.&#160; They take into account the timing and amount of benefits that would be available under the plans.  The Company&#x2019;s policy is to match the plan&#x2019;s cash flows to that of a hypothetical bond portfolio whose cash flow from coupons and maturities match the plan&#x2019;s projected benefit cash flows.  The discount rates are the single rates that produce the same present value of cash flows.  The selection of the 5.27% and 5.21%&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; discount rates as of year-end 2023 for pension and other benefits, respectively, represents the hypothetical bond portfolio using bonds with an AA or better rating constructed with the assistance of an outside consultant.  &lt;/span&gt;A 100-basis point increase in the discount rate would decrease the projected pension benefit obligation as of February 3, 2024, by approximately $210.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;background:#00ffff;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The Company&#x2019;s assumed pension plan investment return rate was 5.50%&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; in 2023, 2022, and 2021.  The value of all investments in the company-sponsored defined benefit pension plans during the calendar year ended December 31, 2023, net of investment management fees and expenses, increased &lt;/span&gt;8.2% and for fiscal year 2023 investments increased 2.8%&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;.  Historically, the Company&#x2019;s pension plans&#x2019; average rate of return was &lt;/span&gt;4.8% for the &lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:Hidden_oT4Ds8j45EqPIz-4YIkHqw;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;font-weight:normal;"&gt;10&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; calendar years ended December 31, 2023, net of all investment management fees and expenses.  For the past &lt;/span&gt;20 years, the Company&#x2019;s pension plans&#x2019; average annual rate of return has been 7.1%&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;.  To determine the expected rate of return on pension plan assets held by the Company, the Company considers current and forecasted plan asset allocations as well as historical and forecasted rates of return on various asset categories.  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;background:#00ffff;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;The Company calculates its expected return on plan assets by using the market-related value of plan assets.  The market-related value of plan assets is determined by adjusting the actual fair value of plan assets for gains or losses on plan assets.  Gains or losses represent the difference between actual and expected returns on plan investments for each plan year.  Gains or losses on plan assets are recognized evenly over a &lt;/span&gt;five-year&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt; period.  Using a different method to calculate the market-related value of plan assets would provide a different expected return on plan assets.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="visibility:hidden;background:#00ffff;"&gt;&#x200b;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;text-indent:18pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;The pension benefit unfunded status decreased in 2023, compared to 2022, due primarily to an increase in discount rates, which lowered the benefit obligation more than the plan&#x2019;s lower actual rate of return versus expected rate of return on assets.&lt;span style="white-space:pre-wrap;"&gt;  The Company&#x2019;s Qualified Plans were fully funded as of February 3, 2024 and January 28, 2023.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p style="font-family:'Times New Roman','Times','serif';font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;"&gt;&lt;span
